title: Why Alternation Speeds Up Counterfactual Regret Minimization?

paper.title: Why Alternation Speeds Up Counterfactual Regret Minimization?
paper.abstract:
Abstract Solving imperfect-information games at scale rests on counterfactual regret minimization
with the regret matching + (RM + ) update, and a seemingly minor implementation choice accounts for much of
its practical speed: alternating the two players’ updates, so that the second
player responds to the strategy the first player just produced. A widely repeated
intuition explains why: seeing the opponent’s fresh strategy should act like optimism. We
treat this intuition as a testable hypothesis about deterministic two-player zero-sum
self-play dynamics and find that its canonical additive form fails an information-matched
test. On an analytic witness family we compare alternating RM + against a one-sided
predictive RM + that receives the same information channel each round and differs only
in where the fresh signal enters, a persistent regret state versus a transient prediction
term. Our main result is a dichotomy theorem that reduces trajectory separation to the
recurrence of exact-vertex play by the predictive dynamics: under an interior-band
assumption on the alternating iterate, either vertex times recur and the profile distance
is at least, infinitely often, an explicit constant that our measurements nearly attain, or they
terminate. Both antecedents are observed throughout the tested range and under multi-precision
recomputation, and a proof of either remains open. The mechanism is a readout dichotomy:
a transient injection at small persistent state turns the readout into a switch between exact vertices, while a
persistent injection is averaged into a rotation whose angular step vanishes as the
regret mass accumulates. Beyond one-sided prediction, a falsification suite over 47 matrix games and
three extensive-form witnesses rules out
the canonical implementations of three further dominant explanation routes, play-level
proximal damping, staleness interpolation, and standard two-sided optimism, whose
relative ordering crosses sign across regimes. Across the tested self-play regimes, any
correct explanation of the alternation speedup must reproduce a staleness cost present at
the smallest tested stale fraction, an advantage that persists across seven orders of payoff conditioning, regime
crossings of the optimism family, and a measured per-perturbation cost of weakening the
injection path that is far steeper for staleness than for
partial persistence.

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
sections.text: Counterfactual regret minimization (CFR) with the regret matching + (RM + ) update rule is the workhorse of large-scale imperfect-information game solving ( Zinkevich et al., 2007 ; Tammelin, 2014 ; Bowling et al., 2015 ; Moravčík et al., 2017 ; Brown and Sandholm, 2018 ) . A seemingly minor implementation choice is responsible for a large share of its practical speed. Alternating the two players’ updates lets the second player respond to the strategy the first player just produced; under simultaneous updates both players respond only to the previous joint profile ( Tammelin, 2014 ; Tammelin et al., 2015 ; Burch et al., 2019 ; Brown and Sandholm, 2019 ) . The speedup is robust, routinely one to two orders of magnitude, and largely unexplained. Existing theory separates the alternating duality gap from the simultaneous one by a nonnegative improvement term ( Burch et al., 2019 ) , while the best known regret bounds for predictive regret matching do not separate them ( Hait et al., 2025 ) . There is, however, a folk explanation. Under alternation, player 2’s update sees player 1’s fresh strategy; a simultaneous update would see the one before it. Seeing the opponent’s next move is what optimistic or predictive no-regret methods approximate with a prediction term ( Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013a ; Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013b ; Syrgkanis et al., 2015 ) , and predictive variants of regret matching carry exactly this prediction term ( Farina et al., 2019a ; Farina et al., 2021 ) . The reading of alternation as optimism with a perfect one-step predictor is natural enough that, to our knowledge, it has never been isolated and tested directly. We isolate it here, and its canonical additive form fails the test. We study the self-play dynamical system : the deterministic sequence of profiles and duality gaps generated when both players run a fixed update rule against each other. This object is distinct from the adversarial alternating-regret setting, whose lower bounds ( Hait et al., 2025 ) do not settle self-play trajectory equivalence. We ask whether the alternation speedup can be reproduced by the optimism family. The core difficulty in testing the folk explanation is a confound: an optimistic method differs from alternation in which information it uses and in how it uses it. We remove the confound by construction. On an analytic family of 2 × 2 2\times 2 zero-sum games we compare two dynamics that receive the same information channel every round, player 2’s instantaneous regret against player 1’s newly computed strategy, evaluated along each dynamics’ own trajectory. The two dynamics differ in one respect. Alternating RM + ( alt ) folds this signal into the persistent regret state. One-sided predictive RM + ( os-prm + ), the canonical additive realization of “alternation as optimism,” injects it as a transient prediction term discarded after each round. If the folk explanation were right, the two should be close. Their duality gaps separate by a factor of 5 5 to 154 154 (median 28.7 28.7 ) across the family, and their trajectories remain a constant distance apart on average (median final ℓ 1 \ell_{1} 0.58 0.58 ). Our main theorem turns this into mathematics. The alternating player’s strategy stays bounded away from exact vertices by a margin, verified on the tested grid in every arithmetic precision, and under this interior-band assumption the comparison reduces to the recurrence of the predictive dynamics’ exact-vertex play. The local analysis exposes the mechanism ( Fig. 1 ): a transient injection meets a persistent state that the dynamics itself washes down to exactly zero, so the readout becomes an unbounded-gain switch between exact vertices, while a persistent injection is averaged by a growing normalizer into a rotation whose angular step vanishes as the regret mass grows. One-sided prediction is only the most literal reading of the folk explanation. We assemble the dominant live explanation routes into a falsification catalog of four mechanism families, labeled F1 to F4: canonical additive one-sided prediction (F1), play-level proximal damping of the alternating structure (F2), staleness interpolation, alternation read as a fresher simultaneous update (F3), and standard two-sided optimism in its three standard implementations (F4). Each family comes with its implied signature and a pre-registered falsifier, and all four canonical implementations fail on a suite of 47 47 matrix games and extensive-form witnesses (Kuhn poker, Leduc poker, and a liar’s-dice game). Our contributions are as follows. • We prove a conditional trajectory-level separation of alternation from one-sided optimism. On an analytic witness family the canonical additive predictive form either revisits exact vertices infinitely often, in which case its distance from the alternating trajectory is at least an explicit constant infinitely often, a constant our measurements nearly attain, or its vertex play terminates. Both antecedents are observed on the tested grid ( Section 5 ). • We identify the mechanism behind the speedup and quantify it. An exact decomposition of the alternating duality gap isolates a nonnegative improvement term with a closed form under plain RM + , equal on truncation-free windows to at least a 1 / m 1/\sqrt{m} fraction of the increase of the potential that bounds the regret. On the full suite the regret channel accounts for a median share of 0.60 0.60 of the alternating/simultaneous ( alt / sim ) log-speedup, and the one-sided predictive variant’s cost falls on its opponent’s regret on 42 / 47 42/47 games ( Section 5 , Table 4 ). • We test the canonical implementations of the four dominant explanation routes against alternation and find none equivalent. The differences are structured: the two-sided optimism family’s advantage reverses across conditioning and tree regimes, while the price of perturbing alternation is measured: removing half the persistence costs as little as one percent of staleness ( Section 4 , Section 6 , Section 7 ).

sections.heading: 2. Related Work
sections.text: For gradient-type dynamics alternation is provably beneficial: alternating mirror descent improves the average regret of both players ( Wibisono et al., 2022 ) ; alternating gradient descent-ascent admits finite-regret and cycling analyses with near-optimal local rates ( Bailey et al., 2020 ; Zhang et al., 2022 ) , beats simultaneous updates ( Lee et al., 2024 ) , weakens the effective adversary ( Cevher et al., 2023 ) , and attains O ⁡ ( 1 / T ) O(1/T) average-iterate convergence in constrained bilinear games ( Nan et al., 2026 ) . All concern mirror-descent or gradient-descent-ascent updates; whether regret-matching-type dynamics enjoy analogous benefits remains open. We constrain its shape. In the adversarial model, Hait et al. (2025) prove Ω ⁡ ( T ) \Omega(\sqrt{T}) lower bounds on alternating regret for predictive regret matching + ( prm + ) and optimistic gradient methods. For an alternation-aware Hedge variant, Tao and Zheng (2026) prove logarithmic-in- d d bounds on alternating regret with a matching lower bound, and average-iterate convergence at O ⁡ ( log ⁡ d / T ) O(\log d/T) to Nash (zero-sum) and coarse correlated (general-sum) equilibria. These guarantees concern one learner’s worst-case regret under an alternating accounting. Our object is RM + self-play trajectories. In RM + self-play the alternating arm leads the information-matched predictive arm ( Section 5 ). Fictitious play separates the same two mechanisms in the opposite direction. Without regularization, optimism alone attains constant regret on 2 × 2 2\times 2 zero-sum games with a unique interior equilibrium under any tiebreaking rule, while alternation alone incurs Ω ⁡ ( T ) \Omega(\sqrt{T}) regret on Matching Pennies for almost all initializations ( Lazarsfeld et al., 2026 ) . Our witness family lives in exactly that game class, so the contrast isolates the update rule. Optimistic no-regret methods exploit predictable loss sequences ( Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013a ; Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013b ) , and the Regret bounded by Variation in Utilities (RVU) property converts prediction into fast convergence ( Syrgkanis et al., 2015 ) . Predictive Blackwell approachability transfers this machinery to regret matching ( prm + , Blackwell, 1956 ; Farina et al., 2021 ); optimistic variants extend it to sequential games ( Farina et al., 2019a ; Farina et al., 2019b ) and to weighted, discounted regret ( Xu et al., 2024b ) , refined forms of optimism improve rates in general games ( Soleymani et al., 2025 ) , and adaptive asymmetry of step sizes stabilizes predictive CFR under inaccurate predictions ( Meng et al., 2026a ) . In the simultaneous regime the same route has reached constant regret: Liu et al. (2026) bound each player’s individual regret independently of the horizon in N N -player general-sum self-play, via an exponential moving average (EMA) cascade optimism of a form our two-sided falsifier does not target. These works supply the optimistic machinery that our one-sided and two-sided families formalize, and alt ’s measured behavior contradicts both signatures. Neither RM + nor prm + is last-iterate stable in general: strategies can cycle while averages converge ( Farina et al., 2023 ) , the last-iterate landscape is delicate ( Cai et al., 2025a ; Fiegel et al., 2025 ) , and fast last-iterate convergence provably requires forgetting ( Cai et al., 2024 ) . For optimistic dynamics the three notions separate outright: a uniform best-iterate rate is available where uniform last-iterate and polynomial random-iterate rates are not ( Cai et al., 2026 ) . Smooth, constrained, or perturbed variants recover guarantees ( Daskalakis and Panageas, 2019 ; Wei et al., 2021 ; Abe et al., 2023 ; Meng et al., 2025 ) , and optimistic regret minimization over treeplexes recovers them in sequential games ( Lee et al., 2021 ) . The limit points of optimistic gradient methods are characterized by Daskalakis and Panageas (2018) , reductions carry average-iterate results to the last iterate ( Cai et al., 2025b ) , and optimistic multiplicative weights converge in the last iterate under smoothness ( Orabona, 2026 ) . The separation between plain regret matching and RM + is itself sharpening: in two-player potential games RM + converges while regret matching may need exponentially many iterations ( Anagnostides et al., 2026 ) , and self-bounding forms tighten the regret envelope of RM + ( Dewasurendra and Jayawardhana, 2026 ) . Running-average references restore last-iterate convergence in self-play ( Savcı, 2026 ) ; parameter-free and scale-invariant variants of regret matching accelerate average-iterate play ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Meng et al., 2026b ) , and a scale-invariant extragradient variant of regret matching converges linearly in the last iterate under a norm-saturation condition ( Li and Huang, 2026g ) . We contribute a sharp instance: on the witness family, at finite horizon, the one-sided predictive dynamics exhibits a bang–bang vertex-visiting mode with its persistent state washed to exactly zero, while alternation rotates with a shrinking step ( Section 5 ). Alternation entered practice with CFR+ ( Tammelin, 2014 ; Tammelin et al., 2015 ; Bowling et al., 2015 ) , was analyzed for correctness by Burch et al. (2019) , and is a default in modern discounted variants ( Brown and Sandholm, 2019 ; Xu et al., 2024a ) . Recent work scales the practice up: parallel and real-time solvers ( Li and Huang, 2026d ; Li and Huang, 2026f ) , pruning and learned or large language model (LLM)-generated abstraction ( Li et al., 2024 ; Li and Huang, 2025 ; Li and Huang, 2026a ; Li and Huang, 2026c ) , and tooling for Monte Carlo sampling, certification, evaluation, and tournaments ( Li et al., 2026a ; Li et al., 2026b ; Li and Huang, 2026b ; Li and Huang, 2026e ) .

sections.heading: 4. Mechanisms
sections.text: We formalize the dominant live explanation routes for the alternation speedup, in the literature and in folklore. Each route is a mechanism family with a testable signature; we label the four families F1 to F4 in the order they appear below. Table 1 summarizes the catalog; the arms’ exact update rules are given in Appendix D . sections.heading: 7. Findings
sections.text: The catalog’s failures leave measured regularities, scoped to the tested self-play regimes (47-game suite; Kuhn, Leduc, liar’s dice). Staleness is expensive down to the smallest tested fraction. Let s s be the stale fraction of the information player 2 uses, so s = 1 − θ s=1-\theta for the mixing dial mix ​ ( θ ) \textsc{mix}(\theta) and s = d s=d for the integer delay family. On the mixing branch the median gap ratio to alt is fit by gap / gap ALT − 1 ≈ 36 ​ s 0.67 \mathrm{gap}/\mathrm{gap}_{\mathrm{ALT}}-1\approx 36\,s^{0.67} over s ∈ [ 0.01 , 1 ] s\in[0.01,1] (log-space least squares, largest deviation 25 % 25\% ; Fig. 4 ); on the delay branch it grows slightly faster than linearly (median per-game per-doubling ratio 1.9 → 2.4 1.9\to 2.4 from d = 2 d=2 to 16 16 ). One percent of staleness already costs 2.6 × 2.6\times (median; within 3 × 3\times of alt on 26 / 47 26/47 games), and 100 % 100\% costs 41 × 41\times . Any theory of alternation as “a slightly fresher simultaneous update” must reproduce this cost at s = 0.01 s=0.01 . The speedup survives payoff conditioning. Across seven orders of magnitude of condition number the alt advantage over sim never falls below 13.5 × 13.5\times and shows no monotone trend (medians 13.5 13.5 to 149.1 149.1 across the eight bands), while optimism-family acceleration closes at κ ∗ ≈ 10 5 \kappa^{*}\approx 10^{5} – 10 6 10^{6} and partially reverses. Optimism’s advantage comes and goes with the regime, while alternation’s holds throughout. At the suite-median level the alt / sim ratio is ≥ 13.5 × \geq 13.5\times at every κ \kappa , 119 × 119\times on Kuhn, 321 × 321\times on Leduc, and 8 8 / 5.1 5.1 / 3.1 × 3.1\times on the three liar’s-dice trees. The two-sided optimism arms beat alt on well-conditioned matrix games and on Kuhn ( prm + 14 × 14\times , pp 520 × 520\times faster), lose to it on Leduc ( 19 19 – 70 × 70\times slower), prm + reverses to 3.9 × 3.9\times and 2.7 × 2.7\times slower at κ = 10 7 , 10 8 \kappa=10^{7},10^{8} , pp is within 1.22 × 1.22\times of alt at κ = 10 6 , 10 7 \kappa=10^{6},10^{7} , and ts-opt never falls behind, and os-prm + straddles it on liar’s dice ( 0.98 × 0.98\times at 51,176 51{,}176 nodes, 1.09 × 1.09\times at 294,877 294{,}877 ). An arm whose dynamics coincided with alt ’s could not change sign relative to it across these regimes. Weakening the fresh signal costs less when the injection path is degraded than when freshness is. Under the median criterion every dial reaches alt at its limit, and the cost at the smallest setting is 2.6 × 2.6\times for 1 % 1\% staleness, 1.66 × 1.66\times for 0.1 % 0.1\% damping, and 1.65 × 1.65\times for a 50 % 50\% loss of persistence. Removing half the persistence is as cheap as removing one percent of the freshness; short of the alt endpoint, only the injection dial puts 90 % 90\% of games within 3 × 3\times , from μ = 0.75 \mu=0.75 on ( Table 18 ). Freshness is the expensive resource, and any explanation must reproduce this cost curve. With the conditional certificate of Theorem 2 , these four regularities form a checklist for explanations of the speedup. Positions untouched by the four comparisons include persistent auxiliary prediction states outside F1, non-RVU stabilization, and per-round fresh-information analyses, as the staleness cost supports.

sections.heading: 8. Conclusion
sections.text: The folk explanation of the alternation speedup, seeing the opponent’s fresh strategy as optimism, fails an information-matched test. On the 2 × 2 2\times 2 witness family, under an interior-band assumption on the alternating iterate, either exact-vertex times of the predictive dynamics recur and the profile distance is at least a constant between 0.53 0.53 and 0.91 0.91 infinitely often, or they terminate; the antecedents hold on all 60 grid points at 2 × 10 5 2\times 10^{5} iterations across four precisions. The mechanism is a readout dichotomy: transient injection at small persistent state produces an unbounded-gain bang–bang readout, persistent injection a rotation whose angular step vanishes as the measured regret mass grows. Three further routes (play-level damping, staleness interpolation, two-sided optimism) are not reproduced in canonical implementations on the 47-game suite and tree witnesses, and weakening them costs more when freshness is lost than when the injection path is degraded. Within the tested regimes, alternation is not optimism.

sections.text: This appendix documents the pre-registered claim ladder, the empirical failure of its top rung, and the three proof routes attempted before the dichotomy theorem closed. We include it because negative-result papers are only as credible as their disclosure discipline.

sections.heading: C.1. The ladder and its gates
sections.text: The ladder of Section 3 was frozen before any theorem-directed experiment ran, together with operational gates: the strong-separation rung (ii) required, on the 60-point witness scan, a nonempty parameter interval where min t ⁡ D t \min_{t}D_{t} over the tail half stays ≥ 0.2 \geq 0.2 while the windowed mean does not decay. The frozen pre-registration file and the dated experiment tracker will be released with the code upon acceptance.

sections.heading: Gate outcome (rung (ii) fails).
sections.text: The scan ( a ∈ [ 1.05 , 4 ] a\in[1.05,4] , 60 points, T = 2 × 10 4 T=2\times 10^{4} ) produced: windowed means of D t D_{t} flat at 0.60 0.60 – 1.06 1.06 on all 60 points (no decay anywhere, fourth-quarter vs third-quarter window ratio ≥ 0.8 \geq 0.8 on 60/60), but tail minima with median 0.012 0.012 and minimum 3.4 × 10 − 4 3.4\times 10^{-4} ; only two isolated grid points ( a = 3.15 , 3.65 a=3.15,3.65 ) met the ≥ 0.2 \geq 0.2 criterion, and no two adjacent grid points did. Deep runs at T = 10 6 T=10^{6} pushed tail minima lower still ( ∼ 4 × 10 − 4 \sim 4\times 10^{-4} ). Mechanism (measured): alt ’s rotation periodically sweeps past os-prm + ’s vertex–uniform jump set, so on every tested horizon the tail minimum of D t D_{t} falls well below 0.2 0.2 even though the process spends most of its time at D t = Θ ⁡ ( 1 ) D_{t}=\Theta(1) . sections.heading: Final placement.
sections.text: The result landed between the pre-registered rungs: a rigorous dichotomy theorem with one finite-horizon verified assumption and an explicit, empirically tight constant. This is stronger than the pre-registered fallback for total proof failure (formalized conjecture plus witness family), and weaker than an unconditional rung-(iii) theorem; Conjecture 1 records the remaining gap precisely.

sections.heading: C.3. Exact-arithmetic validation
sections.text: As a check that the early dynamics are not floating-point artifacts (the four-precision recomputation of Table 14 covers long horizons statistically), the first iterations of both dynamics were replayed in exact rational arithmetic at five representative values of a a . The rational and float trajectories agree to 10 − 12 10^{-12} for as long as the rational replay is feasible. Feasibility ends quickly, since denominator bit-lengths roughly double per iteration (reaching 10 4.5 10^{4.5} – 10 5 10^{5} bits by t = 9 t=9 – 10 10 ), so the exact replay covers the early iterations only. Symbolic itineraries (truncation-activity patterns of both dynamics) over long floating-point runs use at most 8 distinct symbols, with alt eventually truncation-free (consistent with Lemma 8 ’s regime) and os-prm + showing persistent-state zeroing in 88 88 – 100 % 100\% of tail windows plus exact-vertex visits at frequency 51 51 – 66 % 66\% on these five points ( Appendix E ).

sections.heading: C.4. Scope of the claims
sections.text: Our claims are scoped to deterministic self-play dynamics of the tested update rules, not to sampled (Monte Carlo) variants, discounted weighting ( Brown and Sandholm, 2019 ) , or adversarial training loops. The theorem is for a 2 × 2 2\times 2 family, and the extensive-form evidence is witness-level, with one pre-registered gate failure ( Section 6 ). Leduc-scale trees are far from the game sizes where alternation’s value was first observed ( Bowling et al., 2015 ) . The catalog covers the dominant live routes, not all conceivable explanations, and the staleness and damping dials are tested down to s = λ = 10 − 2 s=\lambda=10^{-2} and 10 − 3 10^{-3} only. Tree distances are per information set, not reach-weighted. Excluding branch (b) would require proving that os-prm + plays exact vertices infinitely often, a property stronger than last-iterate non-convergence and adjacent to the known instability of prm + -family last iterates ( Farina et al., 2023 ; Cai et al., 2025a ) . We offer no positive theory. The most natural candidate, play-level proximal damping, reproduces alt at its three weakest tested settings ( λ ≤ 0.005 \lambda\leq 0.005 ) and at a cost that grows with the perturbation.

Boning Li Affiliation: Institute for Interdisciplinary Information Sciences, Tsinghua University Correspondence: longbohuang@tsinghua.edu.cn Longbo Huang October 15, 2026 Abstract Solving imperfect-information games at scale rests on counterfactual regret minimization with the regret matching + (RM + ) update, and a seemingly minor implementation choice accounts for much of its practical speed: alternating the two players’ updates, so that the second player responds to the strategy the first player just produced. A widely repeated intuition explains why: seeing the opponent’s fresh strategy should act like optimism. We treat this intuition as a testable hypothesis about deterministic two-player zero-sum self-play dynamics and find that its canonical additive form fails an information-matched test. On an analytic witness family we compare alternating RM + against a one-sided predictive RM + that receives the same information channel each round and differs only in where the fresh signal enters, a persistent regret state versus a transient prediction term. Our main result is a dichotomy theorem that reduces trajectory separation to the recurrence of exact-vertex play by the predictive dynamics: under an interior-band assumption on the alternating iterate, either vertex times recur and the profile distance is at least, infinitely often, an explicit constant that our measurements nearly attain, or they terminate. Both antecedents are observed throughout the tested range and under multi-precision recomputation, and a proof of either remains open. The mechanism is a readout dichotomy: a transient injection at small persistent state turns the readout into a switch between exact vertices, while a persistent injection is averaged into a rotation whose angular step vanishes as the regret mass accumulates. Beyond one-sided prediction, a falsification suite over 47 matrix games and three extensive-form witnesses rules out the canonical implementations of three further dominant explanation routes, play-level proximal damping, staleness interpolation, and standard two-sided optimism, whose relative ordering crosses sign across regimes. Across the tested self-play regimes, any correct explanation of the alternation speedup must reproduce a staleness cost present at the smallest tested stale fraction, an advantage that persists across seven orders of payoff conditioning, regime crossings of the optimism family, and a measured per-perturbation cost of weakening the injection path that is far steeper for staleness than for partial persistence. 1. Introduction Counterfactual regret minimization (CFR) with the regret matching + (RM + ) update rule is the workhorse of large-scale imperfect-information game solving ( Zinkevich et al., 2007 ; Tammelin, 2014 ; Bowling et al., 2015 ; Moravčík et al., 2017 ; Brown and Sandholm, 2018 ) . A seemingly minor implementation choice is responsible for a large share of its practical speed. Alternating the two players’ updates lets the second player respond to the strategy the first player just produced; under simultaneous updates both players respond only to the previous joint profile ( Tammelin, 2014 ; Tammelin et al., 2015 ; Burch et al., 2019 ; Brown and Sandholm, 2019 ) . The speedup is robust, routinely one to two orders of magnitude, and largely unexplained. Existing theory separates the alternating duality gap from the simultaneous one by a nonnegative improvement term ( Burch et al., 2019 ) , while the best known regret bounds for predictive regret matching do not separate them ( Hait et al., 2025 ) . There is, however, a folk explanation. Under alternation, player 2’s update sees player 1’s fresh strategy; a simultaneous update would see the one before it. Seeing the opponent’s next move is what optimistic or predictive no-regret methods approximate with a prediction term ( Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013a ; Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013b ; Syrgkanis et al., 2015 ) , and predictive variants of regret matching carry exactly this prediction term ( Farina et al., 2019a ; Farina et al., 2021 ) . The reading of alternation as optimism with a perfect one-step predictor is natural enough that, to our knowledge, it has never been isolated and tested directly. We isolate it here, and its canonical additive form fails the test. We study the self-play dynamical system : the deterministic sequence of profiles and duality gaps generated when both players run a fixed update rule against each other. This object is distinct from the adversarial alternating-regret setting, whose lower bounds ( Hait et al., 2025 ) do not settle self-play trajectory equivalence. We ask whether the alternation speedup can be reproduced by the optimism family. The core difficulty in testing the folk explanation is a confound: an optimistic method differs from alternation in which information it uses and in how it uses it. We remove the confound by construction. On an analytic family of 2 × 2 2\times 2 zero-sum games we compare two dynamics that receive the same information channel every round, player 2’s instantaneous regret against player 1’s newly computed strategy, evaluated along each dynamics’ own trajectory. The two dynamics differ in one respect. Alternating RM + ( alt ) folds this signal into the persistent regret state. One-sided predictive RM + ( os-prm + ), the canonical additive realization of “alternation as optimism,” injects it as a transient prediction term discarded after each round. If the folk explanation were right, the two should be close. Their duality gaps separate by a factor of 5 5 to 154 154 (median 28.7 28.7 ) across the family, and their trajectories remain a constant distance apart on average (median final ℓ 1 \ell_{1} 0.58 0.58 ). Our main theorem turns this into mathematics. The alternating player’s strategy stays bounded away from exact vertices by a margin, verified on the tested grid in every arithmetic precision, and under this interior-band assumption the comparison reduces to the recurrence of the predictive dynamics’ exact-vertex play. The local analysis exposes the mechanism ( Fig. 1 ): a transient injection meets a persistent state that the dynamics itself washes down to exactly zero, so the readout becomes an unbounded-gain switch between exact vertices, while a persistent injection is averaged by a growing normalizer into a rotation whose angular step vanishes as the regret mass grows. One-sided prediction is only the most literal reading of the folk explanation. We assemble the dominant live explanation routes into a falsification catalog of four mechanism families, labeled F1 to F4: canonical additive one-sided prediction (F1), play-level proximal damping of the alternating structure (F2), staleness interpolation, alternation read as a fresher simultaneous update (F3), and standard two-sided optimism in its three standard implementations (F4). Each family comes with its implied signature and a pre-registered falsifier, and all four canonical implementations fail on a suite of 47 47 matrix games and extensive-form witnesses (Kuhn poker, Leduc poker, and a liar’s-dice game). Our contributions are as follows. • We prove a conditional trajectory-level separation of alternation from one-sided optimism. On an analytic witness family the canonical additive predictive form either revisits exact vertices infinitely often, in which case its distance from the alternating trajectory is at least an explicit constant infinitely often, a constant our measurements nearly attain, or its vertex play terminates. Both antecedents are observed on the tested grid ( Section 5 ). • We identify the mechanism behind the speedup and quantify it. An exact decomposition of the alternating duality gap isolates a nonnegative improvement term with a closed form under plain RM + , equal on truncation-free windows to at least a 1 / m 1/\sqrt{m} fraction of the increase of the potential that bounds the regret. On the full suite the regret channel accounts for a median share of 0.60 0.60 of the alternating/simultaneous ( alt / sim ) log-speedup, and the one-sided predictive variant’s cost falls on its opponent’s regret on 42 / 47 42/47 games ( Section 5 , Table 4 ). • We test the canonical implementations of the four dominant explanation routes against alternation and find none equivalent. The differences are structured: the two-sided optimism family’s advantage reverses across conditioning and tree regimes, while the price of perturbing alternation is measured: removing half the persistence costs as little as one percent of staleness ( Section 4 , Section 6 , Section 7 ). 2. Related Work For gradient-type dynamics alternation is provably beneficial: alternating mirror descent improves the average regret of both players ( Wibisono et al., 2022 ) ; alternating gradient descent-ascent admits finite-regret and cycling analyses with near-optimal local rates ( Bailey et al., 2020 ; Zhang et al., 2022 ) , beats simultaneous updates ( Lee et al., 2024 ) , weakens the effective adversary ( Cevher et al., 2023 ) , and attains O ⁡ ( 1 / T ) O(1/T) average-iterate convergence in constrained bilinear games ( Nan et al., 2026 ) . All concern mirror-descent or gradient-descent-ascent updates; whether regret-matching-type dynamics enjoy analogous benefits remains open. We constrain its shape. In the adversarial model, Hait et al. (2025) prove Ω ⁡ ( T ) \Omega(\sqrt{T}) lower bounds on alternating regret for predictive regret matching + ( prm + ) and optimistic gradient methods. For an alternation-aware Hedge variant, Tao and Zheng (2026) prove logarithmic-in- d d bounds on alternating regret with a matching lower bound, and average-iterate convergence at O ⁡ ( log ⁡ d / T ) O(\log d/T) to Nash (zero-sum) and coarse correlated (general-sum) equilibria. These guarantees concern one learner’s worst-case regret under an alternating accounting. Our object is RM + self-play trajectories. In RM + self-play the alternating arm leads the information-matched predictive arm ( Section 5 ). Fictitious play separates the same two mechanisms in the opposite direction. Without regularization, optimism alone attains constant regret on 2 × 2 2\times 2 zero-sum games with a unique interior equilibrium under any tiebreaking rule, while alternation alone incurs Ω ⁡ ( T ) \Omega(\sqrt{T}) regret on Matching Pennies for almost all initializations ( Lazarsfeld et al., 2026 ) . Our witness family lives in exactly that game class, so the contrast isolates the update rule. Optimistic no-regret methods exploit predictable loss sequences ( Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013a ; Rakhlin and Sridharan, 2013b ) , and the Regret bounded by Variation in Utilities (RVU) property converts prediction into fast convergence ( Syrgkanis et al., 2015 ) . Predictive Blackwell approachability transfers this machinery to regret matching ( prm + , Blackwell, 1956 ; Farina et al., 2021 ); optimistic variants extend it to sequential games ( Farina et al., 2019a ; Farina et al., 2019b ) and to weighted, discounted regret ( Xu et al., 2024b ) , refined forms of optimism improve rates in general games ( Soleymani et al., 2025 ) , and adaptive asymmetry of step sizes stabilizes predictive CFR under inaccurate predictions ( Meng et al., 2026a ) . In the simultaneous regime the same route has reached constant regret: Liu et al. (2026) bound each player’s individual regret independently of the horizon in N N -player general-sum self-play, via an exponential moving average (EMA) cascade optimism of a form our two-sided falsifier does not target. These works supply the optimistic machinery that our one-sided and two-sided families formalize, and alt ’s measured behavior contradicts both signatures. Neither RM + nor prm + is last-iterate stable in general: strategies can cycle while averages converge ( Farina et al., 2023 ) , the last-iterate landscape is delicate ( Cai et al., 2025a ; Fiegel et al., 2025 ) , and fast last-iterate convergence provably requires forgetting ( Cai et al., 2024 ) . For optimistic dynamics the three notions separate outright: a uniform best-iterate rate is available where uniform last-iterate and polynomial random-iterate rates are not ( Cai et al., 2026 ) . Smooth, constrained, or perturbed variants recover guarantees ( Daskalakis and Panageas, 2019 ; Wei et al., 2021 ; Abe et al., 2023 ; Meng et al., 2025 ) , and optimistic regret minimization over treeplexes recovers them in sequential games ( Lee et al., 2021 ) . The limit points of optimistic gradient methods are characterized by Daskalakis and Panageas (2018) , reductions carry average-iterate results to the last iterate ( Cai et al., 2025b ) , and optimistic multiplicative weights converge in the last iterate under smoothness ( Orabona, 2026 ) . The separation between plain regret matching and RM + is itself sharpening: in two-player potential games RM + converges while regret matching may need exponentially many iterations ( Anagnostides et al., 2026 ) , and self-bounding forms tighten the regret envelope of RM + ( Dewasurendra and Jayawardhana, 2026 ) . Running-average references restore last-iterate convergence in self-play ( Savcı, 2026 ) ; parameter-free and scale-invariant variants of regret matching accelerate average-iterate play ( Zhang et al., 2025 ; Meng et al., 2026b ) , and a scale-invariant extragradient variant of regret matching converges linearly in the last iterate under a norm-saturation condition ( Li and Huang, 2026g ) . We contribute a sharp instance: on the witness family, at finite horizon, the one-sided predictive dynamics exhibits a bang–bang vertex-visiting mode with its persistent state washed to exactly zero, while alternation rotates with a shrinking step ( Section 5 ). Alternation entered practice with CFR+ ( Tammelin, 2014 ; Tammelin et al., 2015 ; Bowling et al., 2015 ) , was analyzed for correctness by Burch et al. (2019) , and is a default in modern discounted variants ( Brown and Sandholm, 2019 ; Xu et al., 2024a ) . Recent work scales the practice up: parallel and real-time solvers ( Li and Huang, 2026d ; Li and Huang, 2026f ) , pruning and learned or large language model (LLM)-generated abstraction ( Li et al., 2024 ; Li and Huang, 2025 ; Li and Huang, 2026a ; Li and Huang, 2026c ) , and tooling for Monte Carlo sampling, certification, evaluation, and tournaments ( Li et al., 2026a ; Li et al., 2026b ; Li and Huang, 2026b ; Li and Huang, 2026e ) . 3.
